class: A matching rule built around one person's field (a default list of network titles, and technical words like network/cloud/security) lets in the wrong jobs for the owner and gives nothing to anyone else
symptom: The suggested-jobs list held Senior Software Engineer (Backend), Staff Application Security Engineer, Sr. Data Engineer and mobile roles for a network and cloud-security engineer, and only about 114 open jobs overall.
site: Dashboard suggested jobs (greenhouse, lever, ashby, workday boards), 2 November 2026
root_cause: calculate_match_score gave 20 points to any title with 'engineer' plus a technical word, then added remote (30) and senior (10), reaching the cut-off with no title of the person's. Titles were few (the resume draft kept 3) and a default list of network titles lived in code.
why_tests_missed: The ranking tests checked that a targeted title outranks a loose one, never that the loose one should not be suggested at all, and used only the owner's kind of profile.
fix: Only a person's own target_titles match (the resume draft now proposes up to 12). Titles naming another discipline, or a word in the new avoid_title_words profile field, score 0 unless the person's titles use them; a person whose titles name a discipline is not subject to the built-in list. The default title list was removed from load_profile.
prevention: Build every matching rule from the person's profile and resume; test each rule with at least two unlike profiles (a network engineer and a software engineer), never one.
